newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Pertamina calls for private LPG investment.
newsitem.headline: Pertamina calls for private LPG investment.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina on Thursday called on investors to help develop the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) industry in Indonesia to anticipate expanding markets in the Asia-Pacific region.

"We would like to invite interested parties to participate in developing the LPG business in Indonesia, and to become our partners to exploit the opportunities in expanding markets in the Asia-Pacific region," Pertamina President Director Faisal Abda'oe said in an opening address at the World LPG Forum in Bali.
He said demand for LPG was growning at an annual average of 6.3 percent in the Asia-Pacific region.
Pertamina would continue to increase the role of LPG in its domestic and regional markets.
"We will continue developing and utilising gas potential to enhance the utilisation of LPG in domestic and regional markets.
"We escalate our exploration campaigns to find new additional natural gas reserves in frontier areas and deep seas, especially in the Indonesian eastern region.
"In addition, we develop marginal gas fields and build mini LPG plants to satisfy local needs," Abda'oe said.
He said Indonesia currently produced around 3.0 million tonnes of LPG a year, of which more than 75 percent was exported.
Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said in May the country had reserves of 115 trillion standard cubic feet of gas.

Abda'oe also said he welcomed the decision of the World LPG Forum to change its name to the World LPG Association at the Bali meeting. The forum was founded in Dublin in 1987 to promote the use of LPG.
